newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania pension system to end tobacco stock purchases.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania pension system to end tobacco stock purchases.

text.p: The Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System said Friday it would not purchase additional tobacco stocks, citing expected stock volatility and uncertainty surrounding the proposed national settlement with the industry.
State Treasurer Barbara Hafer had recommended the move as part of her push to divest all state pension portfolios of tobacco stocks.
PSERS is the largest of three Pennsylvania state funds.
The move, announced at a board meeting, means PSERS will not increase the $264 million of tobacco stocks it held as of May 30.
Hafer called that "a good first step."

She said in a statement, "While I support this action, I continue to believe we should dump all our tobacco stocks, both because of their volatility and because it's wrong for public funds to profit at the expense of public health."
In addition to PSERS holdings, the State Employees' Retirement System held $76.4 million of tobacco stocks as of May 30 and the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement System held $2.3 million.
